learningObjective: Follow one query block as key and value blocks stream through SRAM tiles, updating softmax state without materializing the full score matrix.
mediumRationale: The Mermaid flow makes the standard HBM round trip legible, while the authored SVG makes the tiled matrix and SRAM residency spatially legible.

pages.insight: The source slide contrasts standard attention with tiled SRAM execution and highlights repeated HBM traffic as the bottleneck.

deckReview.notes: The deck's standard-versus-FlashAttention contrast establishes the right two-view teaching sequence. The web lesson now keeps both views: HBM traffic as a flow and SRAM residency as a deterministic tiled matrix.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
sources.usage: Used to verify the HBM/SRAM data-movement claim and exact tiled-attention framing. The site diagram is an original simplified redraw.
sources.license: No paper figure copied; conceptual reference and citation only.

sourceReview.notes: The primary paper supports the mechanism. The web lesson uses an original simplified matrix-and-memory redraw rather than reusing its dense algorithm figure.

agentReview.summary: Recommended retaining Mermaid for the standard dataflow, assigning stable roles to input, transformation, HBM state, and output, and pairing it with a deterministic tile visual for the SRAM loop.

implementation.accessibility: The Mermaid source includes an accessible title and detailed path description. The SVG includes a title, description, labels, arrows, matrix structure, and a direct reading caption; neither view relies on color alone.
